    Application¶

    rn_forge.fastapi.app ¶

    Construct FastAPI applications with the standard rn-forge adapters.

    AppConfig(*, registry=default_registry(), checks=dict[str, Check](), required_checks=(), check_timeout=2.0, realm=None, tracing=True, log=None, liveness_path=LIVENESS_PATH, readiness_path=READINESS_PATH, legacy_liveness_path=LEGACY_LIVENESS_PATH, max_body_bytes=1048576, api_catalog=True, security_headers=True, hsts=False, cors=None) dataclass ¶

    The standard adapter configuration for :class:FastApiApp.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    registry ProblemRegistry

    Domain exception mappings. Register application exceptions before constructing this configuration.

    		 default_registry()
    checks Mapping[str, Check]

    Readiness checks, keyed by their wire-visible names.

    		 dict[str, Check]()
    required_checks Collection[str]

    Check names whose failure returns 503 from the readiness path.

    		 ()
    check_timeout float | None

    Maximum seconds a single readiness check may run.

    		 2.0
    realm str | None

    Optional Bearer authentication realm for problem responses.

    		 None
    tracing bool

    Instrument the application with FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app and, when nothing else has, set a :class:~opentelemetry.instrumentation.propagators.TraceResponsePropagator as the global response propagator.

    		 True
    log Log | None

    Optional sink for problem.server_error events, called for every 5xx problem response with the exception under "exc".

    		 None
    liveness_path str

    The liveness path.

    		 LIVENESS_PATH
    readiness_path str

    The readiness path.

    		 READINESS_PATH
    legacy_liveness_path str | None

    An alias of liveness_path, marked deprecated in the OpenAPI document. None serves no alias.

    		 LEGACY_LIVENESS_PATH
    max_body_bytes int | None

    The largest request body admitted, per RFC 9110 §15.5.14. None disables the limit; uvicorn itself sets none.

    		 1048576
    api_catalog bool

    Serve RFC 9727's /.well-known/api-catalog, pointing at the OpenAPI document and docs UI.

    		 True
    security_headers bool

    Install the OWASP REST Security Cheat Sheet response headers (rn_forge.web.security.API_SECURITY_HEADERS).

    		 True
    hsts bool

    Also add Strict-Transport-Security. Off by default: sending it over plain HTTP tells a browser to refuse a future connection that isn't HTTPS, so it is opt-in for deployments that terminate TLS themselves rather than at a front end that already sets it.

    		 False
    cors CorsPolicy | None

    A CORS policy to install, or None (the default) to install none — the application owns whether it has a CORS policy at all.

    		 None

    FastApiApp(config=None, *, routers=(), lifespan=None, title='FastAPI', description='', version='0.1.0', **fastapi_kwargs) ¶

    Bases: FastAPI

    A :class:fastapi.FastAPI with the standard rn-forge wiring installed.

    FastAPI is inherited rather than wrapped, so @app.get(), add_middleware and the full :class:~fastapi.FastAPI constructor keyword set remain available.

    Initialize the application and install the standard adapters.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    config AppConfig | None

    Standard adapter configuration. Defaults to AppConfig().

    		 None
    routers Sequence[APIRouter]

    Application routers to include in order.

    		 ()
    lifespan Lifespan[FastAPI] | None

    Application startup and shutdown hook.

    		 None
    title str

    OpenAPI document title.

    		 'FastAPI'
    description str

    OpenAPI document description.

    		 ''
    version str

    OpenAPI document version.

    		 '0.1.0'
    **fastapi_kwargs Any

    Forwarded to the :class:fastapi.FastAPI constructor. generate_unique_id_function defaults to :func:operation_id and may be overridden here.

    		 {}

    openapi() ¶

    Return the OpenAPI document, repaired for problem-response accuracy.

    Builds through super().openapi() — which caches the document the way plain :class:~fastapi.FastAPI does — and repairs the cached document exactly once. A consumer subclass adds further repairs by overriding this method and calling super().openapi() first.
